issues.issue: `git show <sha>:<path>` for a commit that DELETED the path fails with empty stdout, which was hashed as sha256(b'') and added to the preserved set: evidence citing the empty-file hash was accepted as 'preserved in history' for any path ever deleted. FIXED: a non-zero git exit is skipped; test_history_evidence_never_accepts_the_empty_hash_for_a_path_that_was_merely_deleted (failed before). Otherwise sound: only bytes exactly equal (sha256) to a blob committed at that very path in HEAD's history are accepted, so a never-committed or tampered file is still CRITICAL; content committed and then swapped is accepted by design because the cited bytes remain verifiable in git. Limit: only the last 200 commits touching the path (older versions read as drift: fail-safe).
